 MATCHDAY PREVIEW presented by Kiesland | FC Cincinnati visit Orlando City SC for Wild Card game showdown
 Staff Writer
 Carter Chapley
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 The 2026 MLS Regular Season is over, and FC Cincinnati are heading to the MLS Cup Playoffs as they travel to Inter & Co. Stadium in Orlando, Florida, to take on Orlando City SC in a win-or-go-home Wildcard Playoff game on Thursday night. The winner of Thursday night’s one-game playoff series advances to the Best-of-3 Round One matchup against Nashville SC, and the loser is sent home and their season is ended. 
 2026 marks the fifth straight season The Orange and Blue have made the MLS Cup Playoffs, and they are one of just four teams in the league to do so. But this is the first time FC Cincinnati have played in the Wild Card round and now face elimination without a result. So the stakes could not be higher, and on top of the do-or-die stakes of the game, FCC have to go on the road for the match, which has been a rare sight for the club since making the MLS Cup Playoffs for the first time in 2022. Since then, FCC have played on the road in the playoffs only five times across four seasons. 
 So with their backs against the wall, FC Cincinnati will need to rise to meet the moment. But as a spot of optimism, FCC have done some of their best work this season when the odds were greatest, and there is belief in this squad's mentality when facing challenging moments. 
 “Yeah, our backs against the wall. But the thing about this group is I feel like we've had a lot of opportunities where we've had our backs against the wall, or it’s the 90th minute and we need a goal, or we need to tie the game, or whatever it is, and I think we've responded well,” FC Cincinnati defender Nick Hagglund said Monday ahead of the team's trip to Orlando. “In the last four games…I think our backs were against the wall there, and we had to get points and had to get results, and I think we did.” 
 "It's the playoffs. Your backs are always against the wall, absolutely. You're going away to Orlando. It's going to be us versus them in that stadium,” Hagglund added. “I think we have to be up for it.”
 FC Cincinnati had some positive results against Orlando City SC earlier this season, first beating them at TQL Stadium in May by an eye-popping 6-2 scoreline, then earning a 1-1 draw in their visit to Orlando in August, but felt they should have taken more than just a point from that game. 
 But as preparation ramps up for the Wildcard matchup, those previous results bring nothing to the table for FC Cincinnati, and they will be preparing for a totally different kind of game this time around. 
 “To be honest, like whatever happened in the regular season or previous, I think that every team's a little bit different,” Hagglund explained. “So this game will just be about doing whatever it takes. I think we've kind of been in this mode for the last month. Like whatever it takes to get the ball over the line and just survive in advance. The game looks pretty or the game looks ugly. Doesn't matter to us. Whatever the scoreline is is all that matters. I think for us as a group, we've had that mentality for the last month, and I think we're going to just continue to build off that.” 
 The winner of this Wild Card game would turn it around quickly and travel to play Nashville SC on Sunday, November 22, at Geodis Park to start the Round One Best-of-3 series against the Supporters’ Shield winners. Game 2 would come back to the winners' home grounds on Saturday, November 28, before a potential Game 3 returns to Nashville on Wednesday, December 2 (if necessary).
 FC Cincinnati at Orlando City SC – Thursday, November 19, 2026 – 7:30 p.m. ET – Inter & Co. Stadium 
 Watch/Stream (English/Spanish): Apple TV
 English Local Radio: Fox Sports 1360
 Spanish Local Radio: La Mega 101.5 FM 
 FC Cincinnati Social Media: X/Twitter , Instagram and Facebook 
 FC Cincinnati Official Mobile App: iOS and Android 
 History vs. Orlando 
 FC Cincinnati are 3-0-2 at Orlando City SC under Head Coach Pat Noonan dating back to a 2-1 win in Orlando on March 12, 2022, which was his first-career win as FCC’s manager.
 All-time, The Orange and Blue and Orlando share a mirrored 5-5-5 record all-time dating back to the two sides first MLS competition in 2019. FCC and Orlando City SC have never met in competition outside of the MLS regular season.
 Playoff History 
 FC Cincinnati return to the MLS Cup Playoffs for the fifth consecutive season and are one of
 four clubs – including Thursday night’s opponent – to have made the postseason each year since 2022 (ORL, LAFC, RSL). 
 Thursday marks The Orange and Blue’s 14th all-time MLS Cup Playoffs match. FC Cincinnati are 6-5-2 in the prior 13 matches, and are 1-1 in match-deciding shootouts.
 FC CINCINNATI MATCH NOTES 
 (Courtesy of FC Cincinnati Communications ) 
 Playoff Openers – FC Cincinnati are perfect, 4-0, in four prior opening matches in the MLS Cup Playoffs.
 After three seasons of beginning in the Round One Best-of-3 Series, Thursday marks the first time since FCC’s first-ever MLS postseason match in 2022 that the Orange and Blue both begin the playoffs in a single-elimination win-or-go-home match, and begin on the road.
 Playoff Experience – FC Cincinnati’s current roster brings 150 total career appearances in the MLS Cup Playoffs.
 15 players return from last season’s team which made the postseason and five players have been on Cincinnati’s roster for each of the past five seasons. Three players on FC Cincinnati’s roster have won MLS Cup previously in their career (Nick Hagglund – 2017 Toronto FC; Alvas Powell – 2014 Portland Timbers; Miles Robinson – 2018 Atlanta United). 
 José Martínez has also played in an MLS Cup Final (2022 Philadelphia Union). Head Coach Pat Noonan (2008 CLB; 2012 and 2014 LA Galaxy) was also part of three cup-winning clubs.
 Records to be broken – Kévin Denkey (39): Four shy of tying Brandon Vazquez for 2nd most all-time in club history. Evander (38): One shy of tying Kévin Denkey for 3rd most in club history and five shy of tying Brandon Vazquez for 2nd most all-time in club history. Pavel Bucha (21): One shy of tying Danni König and Emmanuel Ledesma for 6th most in club history.
 Last Time On… – FC Cincinnati went 1-0-1 against Orlando City SC in MLS play this season. Most recently, the clubs tied 1-1 in August on a humid 90-degree night in Central Florida. FCC’s win at home over Orlando on May 23, the final match before the MLS pause for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, was a historic win for the Orange and Blue. In that match...
 - FC Cincinnati’s 6 goals equaled a club record for goals scored in an MLS match (9/10/22 vs SJ; 7/6/24 vs MIA).
 - FC Cincinnati’s 16 goal contributions (6 G, 10 A) set a new all-time team single-match Record.
 - Evander’s 5 goal contributions (2 G, 3 A) set a new all-time player single-match record. His three assists also equaled a club record.
 - With his 75th career MLS win in his 151st MLS match, Head Coach Pat Noonan tied Brian Schmetzer's MLS-post shootout era record in becoming the fastest coach to reach 75 regular season wins.
 Scouting Orlando City SC (13-14-7, 46 Points, 8th in the Eastern Conference, W-L-D-D-W) 
 Orlando City SC needed final-day heroics to earn their hosting spot in the MLS Cup Playoffs Wild Card round this week, defeating the New England Revolution 1-0 on Decision Day. Thanks to a goal from Braian Ojeda in the 45’ at Inter & Co. Stadium Orlando earned the three points and moved up the table to the eighth seed, earning the right to host FC Cincinnati this Thursday in the one-game playoff to advance. 
 The clean sheet on the final day gave Orlando City SC their fifth shutout of the season, all earned by Canadian Goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau – who is currently on duty with his country at the Concacaf Nations League. Orlando have struggled to keep clean sheets this year, despite having a strong keeper. In 2026, only one team allowed more goals than Orlando’s 78 conceded (Sporting Kansas City, 81), and their -15 goal differential was sixth worst in MLS because of it.  
 On the offensive side, Orlando was more effective, though, finishing eighth in the league with 63 goals. That offense was led by French international superstar Antoine Griezmann, who joined the side mid-year from Atletico Madrid and still led the team in goal contributions with 22 (14 goals, 8 assists). Argentine midfielder Martín Ojeda, in his fourth year with the club, led Orlando in goals with 16.
 Other key contributors include Iván Angulo, a Colombian midfielder, who led the team with 13 assists. Angulo, along with his teammate Tyrese Spicer, is considered one of the fastest players in Major League Soccer, and Orlando uses that speed to its advantage. 
 On defense, an era is nearing its end for Orlando as Robin Jansson, 35, has announced that after eight seasons and over 260 games with the club, he will retire at the end of this season. He is the club's longest-tenured player and logged over 20,000 minutes with the side. 
 Others on the defensive side of the ball include David Brekalo, a centerback from Slovenia who leads defenders in minutes played this season, and fullback Griffin Dorsey, who has added six goal contributions this season, which was also his first with Orlando after five with Houston Dynamo.
 The side is led by Interim Manager Martín Perelman, who took over in March after longtime Head Coach Oscar Pareja was dismissed after more than six years at the helm of Orlando City SC. Perelman, who hails from Argentina, has been with Orlando since 2022 as either an assistant or second-team manager before his promotion.
 Down the stretch, Orlando have set up in some variation of a 4-4-2, but have also flexed to a 4-2-3-1 at times. In that shape, Perelman has mostly deployed Griezmann and Ojeda up top, with Angulo and Croatian international DP Marco Pašalić on the wings of the four-person midfield.
 Orlando was a far better team at home this season, going 10-4-3 at Inter & Co. Stadium, while struggling more on the road with a 3-10-4 record away from home. This season, the Orange and Blue beat FC Cincinnati 6-2 at TQL Stadium and drew 1-1 in Florida.
